neighbor_comparisons.actual_core_read: Read as a spectral lower bound for the edge-isoperimetric number of the square of a graph. The counted theorem (label theorem:lowerboundi(G^2)closed) takes a non-complete regular connected graph G with adjacency eigenvalues lambda_1 >= ... >= lambda_n, defines Lambda as the maximum number of common neighbours of adjacent vertices and M as the maximum number of neighbours of non-adjacent vertices, and splits into three regimes on Lambda - lambda_n against M + lambda_2 and lambda_1, giving a closed-form bound for i(G^2) in each, with the optimal polynomial p = x^2 + (M-Lambda)x or p = x^2 - (lambda_2+lambda_n)x. The proof optimises the general polynomial p = ax^2+bx+c inside the bound i(G^t) >= (p(lambda_1)-Lambda(p))/(2W(p)) of the preceding theorem and compares the resulting rational expressions case by case.
neighbor_comparisons.reason_target_distinct: The neighbour bounds the edge-isoperimetric number of the square of a regular graph by spectral data of that graph: eigenvalues and maximum common-neighbour counts. Exercise 6.74 bounds the boundary of an arbitrary subset of the finite box {0,...,n-1}^d by a power of its own volume, uniformly in n, with a constant depending only on d. The box graph is not regular across its boundary, and the neighbour states nothing about subsets of a box, about coordinate projections, or about an exponent (d-1)/d. No direction of specialisation connects them, and the neighbour does not claim the box statement.
neighbor_comparisons.title: The optimal polynomial lower bound on the edge-isoperimetric number of the graph square
neighbor_comparisons.source_work: The edge-isoperimetric number of graphs and their powers

neighbor_comparisons.actual_core_read: Read as a counting lemma for small-boundary sets. The counted lemma (label lem:small-boundary-sets) works in a product graph G = square product of connected d_i-regular H_i and states that for n/d^{ln^2 d} <= a <= n/2 the number of vertex sets A of size a with e(A,A^c) < a ln^2 d is at most exp{2a/ln d}. The proof restricts to m = log_2(ln^5 d) coordinates, defines bad sets through coordinate-wise edge counts E_i(A,A^C), and turns the isoperimetric hypothesis into a binomial-product count. The retained context is the companion lemma lem:product-connectivity on the spectral gap of the product.
neighbor_comparisons.reason_target_distinct: The neighbour is a counting statement about how many sets can have a small edge boundary in a product graph, in a size window n/d^{ln^2 d} <= a <= n/2, with an exponential upper bound. Exercise 6.74 is a lower bound on the boundary of one given set, in the full size range below n^d/2, with a volume-power rate and a C_d that the exercise does not name. A bound on the number of small-boundary sets neither implies nor is implied by the per-set volume-to-boundary inequality. The product structure in the neighbour is over arbitrary regular factors and carries no coordinate-projection argument of the Loomis-Whitney kind. Not covering in either direction.
neighbor_comparisons.title: An exponential upper bound on the number of large sets with a small edge boundary in a product graph
neighbor_comparisons.source_work: \vspace{-1.5cm}Perfect Matching in Product Graphs\\ and in their Random Subgraphs

neighbor_comparisons.actual_core_read: Read as a gluing formula for a tree isoperimetric invariant. The counted proposition (label prop:tau-gluing) states that for a domain D obtained by gluing domains D_1,...,D_m at a point p, the total branching excess satisfies tau(D) = sum_i tau(D_i) + (m-1) when p is on the boundary of D and tau(D) = sum_i tau(D_i) - (d-m) otherwise. The proof compares vertex degrees away from p and expands deg_D(p)-1 through the author degree-sum identity to get the (m-1) term.
neighbor_comparisons.reason_target_distinct: The neighbour computes how an additive branching-excess invariant changes under gluing domains in a regular tree. Exercise 6.74 is an inequality between two cardinalities in a finite box. The neighbour has no ambient box, no subset of a lattice, no projection map and no volume-power rate, and its conclusion is an exact identity for its invariant rather than a lower bound for a boundary. Neither statement specialises to the other.
neighbor_comparisons.title: The Isoperimetric Problem in Regular Trees
neighbor_comparisons.source_work: The Isoperimetric Problem in Regular Trees

neighbor_comparisons.actual_core_read: Read as an auxiliary anti-concentration lemma, not as the article slicing bound. The retained counted unit (label lem:almost-indep) states a conditional probability estimate for the bad event of one vertex together with an event E_1(j,t): P[i bad and E_1(j,t)] <= 40000 t log m / (rho_0^2 sqrt(S_j)). Its difficulty reason records that this lemma is printed as not located in the version PDF and that it is delivered with the article own 41-line proof, which conditions on the other alpha_h, sets A = <v_i,v_j> with |A| <= 0.9 and proceeds by estimates. The article title is about hypercube edge slicing, but the slicing result itself is outside the retained span.
neighbor_comparisons.reason_target_distinct: The comparison is with the retained unit only, which is an auxiliary conditional-probability estimate for a bad event in a random hyperplane-family argument on {0,1}^n: a probabilistic upper bound on an intersection of two events. Exercise 6.74 is a deterministic lower bound for the edge boundary of a fixed set A in a box. Even at the level of the article as a whole, a hypercube edge-slicing lower bound concerns how a family of hyperplanes must be arranged to cut every edge, not the boundary size of a single vertex set, so the direction of the statement differs as well (an arrangement count against a per-set isoperimetric inequality). No coverage is claimed, and none is claimed about the article headline result either, which is not in the retained span.

neighbor_comparisons.source_work: Improved lower bound for hypercube edge slicing

neighbor_comparisons.actual_core_read: Read as a slicing-number lower bound for hyperplane covers of the cube. The counted corollary (label cor:slicing) takes a positive integer C and a family of hyperplanes in R^n with normals in {-C,...,C}^n such that every edge of the cube [0,1]^n is sliced by some member, and concludes |H| >= n/(4C). The proof builds H' by adding, for each hyperplane with equation <a,x>=b, the 2C shifted hyperplanes <a,x>=floor(b)+z, checks |H'| <= 2C|H|, and proves through a nested claim that H' meets the nondegeneracy hypothesis of the article main theorem, whence |H'| >= n/2.
neighbor_comparisons.reason_target_distinct: The neighbour lower-bounds the number of hyperplanes needed so that every edge of the cube is sliced at least once: a covering number, quantified as n/(4C) for integer normal vectors bounded by C. Exercise 6.74 lower-bounds the number of edges leaving one fixed vertex set. A slicing family is not a vertex set and its size is not a boundary; the extremal structure in the neighbour is a shift family of parallel hyperplanes indexed by floor(b), and there is no projection, no Loomis-Whitney product and no (d-1)/d exponent. The vocabulary of slicing and the cube is shared, the statements are not.
neighbor_comparisons.title: Nondegenerate hyperplane covers of the hypercube
neighbor_comparisons.source_work: Nondegenerate hyperplane covers of the hypercube

neighbor_comparisons.actual_core_read: Read as a Mazur-map regularity estimate. The counted lemma (label lem:mazur-map-section) takes 1 < p <= 2 with Holder conjugate q, defines J(u) = (|u_1|^{p-2}u_1,...,|u_m|^{p-2}u_m) / ||u||_p^{p-1} as the element of the subdifferential of the q-norm at u satisfying <J(u),u> = ||u||_p, and concludes ||J(u)-J(v)||_q <= 2(||u-v||_p/(||u||_p+||v||_p))^{p-1} for nonzero u,v. The proof establishes a scalar inequality in phi(t)=|t|^{p-2}t with parameters lambda+mu=1, reduces by homogeneity and symmetry to t=1, and integrates the scalar case to the vector estimate. The article title is about volume and projection inequalities, but no such inequality is inside the retained span.
neighbor_comparisons.reason_target_distinct: The neighbour is a quantitative uniform-convexity (Mazur map) estimate between two vectors in R^m, measured in dual L_p norms, valid for 1 < p <= 2. Exercise 6.74 is a combinatorial isoperimetric inequality for subsets of a finite box. There is no vector to differ, no norm, no family of sets and no boundary in the neighbour conclusion, and the neighbour says nothing about cubes or about an exponent (d-1)/d. Despite the article title, the retained unit is not a volume or projection inequality in the Loomis-Whitney family, so the title-level proximity does not produce coverage.

scope_and_evidence_limits: Candidate pool: four bounded LIKE queries over title||difficulty_reason||claim_key in the jep238 master database, LIMIT 60, none truncated; 15 unique metadata hits, of which 6 were exported whole and read, 2 were opened at the header only, and 7 were metadata touches. Only the 6 are compared.

The six exported primaries are arXiv/DOI text units whose work_ref.resolution is unresolved and whose flat items do not exist in this editable package; the SQL claim_key column is NULL for five of the six and the label used for matching comes from the manifest, so no resolved-work, flat-byte or SQL-claim-key claim is made. For the sixth the manifest claim_key and the SQL claim_key agree.

The counted environment is resolved by matching the label text carried by the manifest primary, not the manifest claim_key: for one unit the claim_key is an abbreviated form that does not normalise into its own source label, while the manifest primary quotes the source label verbatim. The rule and the resolved label are recorded per neighbour so the choice can be re-checked.

The manifest locators for these items carry only a primary line span and, for some, context spans; there is no proof span, page list, source map or PDF hash in the manifest, so the proof was read from the exported SQL tex body and no page-level or pixel-level source claim is made.

For two of the six the retained span is not the article headline result (a hypercube edge-slicing paper whose retained unit is an auxiliary anti-concentration lemma, and a volume-and-projection paper whose retained unit is a Mazur-map estimate). The comparison is made against the retained counted statement only; nothing is claimed about the omitted headline results.
No source PDF was opened and no fresh source-pixel evidence is claimed for this semantic task.

This comparison establishes only that no ordinary coverage of Exercise 6.74 appears among the fifteen returned metadata hits and the six read units; it is not a proof of global novelty and not a claim of formal logical independence.
